turns.assessment: The nearly identical +5.3 dB steps in receiver-reported power and estimated OSNR, without a pre-FEC BER, DGD, SOP, far-end, amplifier, or channel-monitor change, point to a receiver-local measurement/calibration anomaly rather than a real optical-path gain change. RX_DEGRADATION is the closest documented mode, but its documented effect is an error penalty and no BER change was observed, so confidence is below the commitment threshold.

proposals.rationale: Only this receiver reports the large correlated power and OSNR steps. Unchanged pre-FEC BER and surrounding optical telemetry make a local receiver/monitoring defect most plausible, although the absence of an RX penalty weakens the documented-mode match.

A channel-selective WSS change could alter one channel's received power without affecting other channels, but the documented mode causes attenuation and low power, opposite to the observed positive step.
Mechanical handling can produce alarm-free power excursions, but it should be brief and generally affect all channels on the span rather than produce a sustained receiver-only level step.
proposals.note: nothing at that location documents the mode
